identification.summary: Crimson Sandstorm (formerly CURIUM) is an Iran-based espionage actor [S1][S2]. Microsoft says it uses a network of fictitious social media accounts to build trust with targets and then delivers malware to exfiltrate data [S1]. Microsoft says it has targeted the defense, maritime shipping, transportation, healthcare and technology sectors, often using watering-hole attacks and social engineering to deliver custom .NET malware. Microsoft also notes earlier research on its malware that used email for command and control [S2]. Microsoft's 2021 CyberWarCon presentation describes CURIUM spending months posing as an attractive woman on LinkedIn or Facebook before sending a malicious document [S3].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft: active since at least 2017 [S2]. Symantec (as Tortoiseshell): active since at least July 2018 (summary of Symantec report via Malpedia) [S4].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Crimson Sandstorm (formerly CURIUM) [S1][S3]. Microsoft states other researchers track it as Tortoiseshell, Imperial Kitten and Yellow Liderc [S2]. Microsoft's profile also lists Houseblend and Tortoise Shell [S1]. PwC tracks it as Yellow Liderc and lists Imperial Kitten, Tortoiseshell, TA456 and Crimson Sandstorm as overlapping names (reported via press) [S8]. Proofpoint tracks TA456 and says it overlaps with Tortoiseshell and Imperial Kitten (reported via press) [S7]. Press coverage of Meta's 2021 takedown says researchers linked much of the activity to Mandiant's UNC1833, with some infrastructure overlap with APT35 [S6]. This is a press claim and is not used to merge clusters. CrowdStrike's IMPERIAL KITTEN is also mapped by Microsoft to Cuboid Sandstorm and Smoke Sandstorm, which Microsoft tracks separately. Facts from CrowdStrike IMPERIAL KITTEN reporting [S9] should therefore be read as the CrowdStrike cluster, not Microsoft's boundary.

attribution.sponsor: Iran. Microsoft assesses Crimson Sandstorm to be connected to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) [S2]. Meta (Facebook) said the malware used in the 2021 Tortoiseshell campaign was developed by Mahak Rayan Afraz, a Tehran IT company with ties to the IRGC (reported via press) [S6]. CrowdStrike assesses that IMPERIAL KITTEN likely fulfills Iranian strategic intelligence requirements associated with IRGC operations (reported via press) [S9].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft describes the actor as 'assessed to be connected to' the IRGC and gives no numeric confidence level [S2]. Its public profile names Iran as country of origin without naming a sponsor [S1]. CrowdStrike uses 'likely' [S9]. In 2019, Symantec and Cisco Talos declined to tie Tortoiseshell to a specific nation-state [S5]. No government attribution of this cluster was found in the sources gathered.
attribution.basis: Microsoft telemetry and its 2024 OpenAI collaboration, which disabled Crimson Sandstorm accounts and assets [S2]. Meta platform investigation and malware-developer attribution [S6]. Vendor victimology and malware analysis from PwC, Proofpoint and CrowdStrike [S7][S8][S9].

objectives: Strategic intelligence collection in support of Iranian (IRGC-associated) requirements [S2][S9]. Targets include US military and defense contractors, IT services firms, and Middle Eastern governments [S1]. The actor uses supply-chain access through IT, engineering and contractor firms to reach their downstream defense and intelligence customers [S1][S4][S7]. Since 2023 it has collected against Israeli and Mediterranean maritime, logistics and technology entities [S8][S9].

sectors: US military personnel and defense contractors [S1][S6]
Aerospace and defense, including smaller subsidiaries of contractors [S6][S7]
IT services and engineering providers to US defense and intelligence agencies [S1]
IT providers in Saudi Arabia (supply chain) [S4]
targeting.notes: Microsoft says that in 2021 the actor spear-phished companies providing IT and engineering services to US defense and intelligence agencies, probably to reach their customers [S1]. Focus shifted from Middle East IT firms (2018-2019) to US military and defense personnel (2019-2021) [S4][S5][S6]. It shifted again to Israeli and Mediterranean shipping, logistics and technology targets (2022-2023) [S8][S9].

capabilities.summary: The actor's signature is long-duration social engineering through fictitious personas on LinkedIn, Facebook and other platforms. It builds trust over months, sends benign media, and then sends a look-alike malicious file [S1][S3][S6][S7]. Lures include fake recruiting and job sites: 'Hire Military Heroes' (2019) delivered a reconnaissance downloader [S5], and a site spoofing a US Labor Department job site was used in 2021 [S6]. The actor runs watering-hole (strategic web compromise) operations that use JavaScript to fingerprint visitors and selectively serve malware [S2][S8][S9]. It also uses macro-laced Excel phishing, credential theft for VPN access, and one-day vulnerability exploitation [S9]. Custom .NET malware includes IMAPLoader, which uses email as C2 and AppDomain Manager Injection [S8], and StandardKeyboard, which uses email C2 and installs as a Windows service [S9]. LEMPO (an updated Liderc) handles persistence, reconnaissance, exfiltration to actor email accounts and artifact deletion [S7]. A Python reverse shell has also been observed [S9]. In 2023 Microsoft observed the actor using LLMs for phishing content, scripting, and defense-evasion code [S2]. In the Symantec-reported Saudi supply-chain intrusions it gained domain-admin access in at least two organizations [S4].

attack.name: Exfiltration Over Asymmetric Encrypted Non-C2 Protocol

campaigns.name: Saudi IT provider supply-chain intrusions (Tortoiseshell)
campaigns.summary: Symantec reports 11 organizations hit, mostly IT providers in Saudi Arabia, in probable supply-chain attacks; domain-admin access in at least two. Activity dates from July 2018 and the report was published in September 2019.

campaigns.name: Hire Military Heroes fake veteran job site
campaigns.summary: Cisco Talos found a fake US veteran hiring site that pushed a downloader collecting system details; it was linked to Tortoiseshell.

campaigns.name: TA456 'Marcella Flores' persona against defense contractor
campaigns.summary: Proofpoint reports a years-long persona relationship with an employee at a small aerospace defense subsidiary. It ended with LEMPO malware delivered in early June 2021.

campaigns.name: Meta takedown of Tortoiseshell personas
campaigns.summary: Meta removed about 200 accounts that used fake recruiter and defense personas to target US military and defense/aerospace personnel. The activity ran since mid-2020 and also reached the UK and Europe. Malware was attributed to IRGC-tied Mahak Rayan Afraz.

campaigns.name: Spear-phishing of IT/engineering firms serving US defense and intelligence
campaigns.summary: Microsoft reports spear-phishing of service providers, probably as a supply-chain route to their government customers.

campaigns.name: Mediterranean maritime watering holes and IMAPLoader
campaigns.summary: PwC reports compromised sites fingerprinting visitors and serving IMAPLoader, focused on Mediterranean maritime, shipping and logistics.

campaigns.name: IMPERIAL KITTEN operations against Israel after 7 October
campaigns.summary: CrowdStrike reports strategic web compromises, phishing and VPN credential theft against Israeli transportation, logistics and technology organizations, using IMAPLoader and StandardKeyboard.

campaigns.name: Microsoft/OpenAI disruption of LLM misuse
campaigns.summary: Microsoft reports Crimson Sandstorm used LLMs for phishing, scripting and evasion code, and disabled its accounts and assets.

diamond.adversary: Iran-based operators that Microsoft assesses to be IRGC-connected [S2]. Meta tied malware development to Mahak Rayan Afraz (reported) [S6].
diamond.capability: Fictitious social-media personas, fake job sites, watering holes with visitor fingerprinting, and macro Excel phishing. Custom .NET malware with email C2 (IMAPLoader, StandardKeyboard, LEMPO/Liderc) [S1][S5][S7][S8][S9].
diamond.infrastructure: Fake persona accounts on Facebook and LinkedIn [S3][S6]. Spoofed recruiting and job domains [S5][S6]. Compromised legitimate websites used as watering holes [S8][S9]. Actor-controlled email accounts used for C2 and exfiltration [S7][S8][S9].
diamond.victim: US military personnel and defense and aerospace contractors. IT service providers in Saudi Arabia and the US defense supply chain. Israeli and Mediterranean shipping, logistics and technology firms. Middle Eastern governments [S1][S4][S6][S8][S9].
diamond.socioPolitical: Iranian strategic intelligence requirements tied to the IRGC. Activity against Israel intensified after the October 2023 Israel-Hamas war [S2][S9].
diamond.technology: Trust in professional social networks and recruiting, the email protocols abused for C2, and third-party IT and contractor access into defense customers [S1][S7][S8].

gaps: MITRE ATT&CK G1012 page could not be fetched (host unreachable); MITRE description and references not verified in this pass.
Primary vendor reports (Symantec 2019, Cisco Talos 2019, Proofpoint 2021, Meta 2021, PwC 2023, CrowdStrike 2023) could not be fetched; content is from press coverage and search-result summaries.

Cluster boundary: CrowdStrike IMPERIAL KITTEN is mapped by Microsoft to Crimson, Cuboid and Smoke Sandstorm. Not every IMPERIAL KITTEN fact (e.g., October 2023 Israel activity) is confirmed by Microsoft as Crimson Sandstorm.

Nimbus Manticore (Check Point, 2025) appears in this record's aliases, but Check Point describes it as overlapping UNC1549/Smoke Sandstorm. Its 2025 European aerospace campaign was excluded pending Microsoft confirmation.
No government (CISA/FBI/DOJ/Treasury) attribution or indictment specific to this cluster was found.
Victim counts and impacts beyond Symantec's 11 organizations and Meta's fewer-than-200 notified individuals are not public.
Activity after February 2024 attributable by Microsoft to Crimson Sandstorm was not found in sources gathered.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (OE): The human and persona layer of cyberspace is key terrain. This includes LinkedIn and Facebook profiles of service members, recruiters and contractor staff, plus third-party IT and engineering providers with access into DoD and intelligence networks [S1][S3][S6]. STEP 2 (effects): Months-long trust building defeats one-time phishing awareness. Email-based C2 blends with normal mail traffic, and watering holes on sector websites let the actor select victims passively [S3][S7][S8][S9]. STEP 3 (adversary template): The template is a fake recruiter or attractive persona, or a compromised sector website with JavaScript fingerprinting. That leads to a lure file or fake job app, then a .NET implant with IMAP/SMTP C2, then reconnaissance and exfiltration to actor email [S5][S7][S8][S9]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued espionage against US defense personnel, contractor subsidiaries, and Israeli and Mediterranean logistics targets through persona-driven social engineering. MDCOA is leveraging compromised IT and engineering providers for supply-chain access into defense or intelligence customer networks, as seen in 2018-2021 [S1][S4]. Candidate indicators: unsolicited recruiter or persona contacts with Airmen or contractors that move to off-platform chat or file sharing [S6][S7]; downloads of 'job' applications [S5]; outbound IMAP from non-mail hosts [S8][S9]; AppDomain Manager Injection artifacts [S8]; and a new 'Keyboard Service' Windows service [S9].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: fuse platform-takedown reporting (Meta, LinkedIn), vendor IOCs for IMAPLoader and StandardKeyboard, and DIB partner reporting into the common operational picture, since the actor's entry points sit outside DoDIN boundaries [S6][S8][S9]. Authorities: persona engagement with personnel on commercial platforms and compromises of contractor networks fall to counterintelligence, the DC3/DIB program and platform providers rather than DODIN defenders alone. Coordinate early [S1][S6]. Mission assurance: prioritize hunting for email-protocol C2 egress and macro and Excel execution on mission systems. Identify contractor and IT service accounts with privileged access as supply-chain risk [S1][S4][S8][S9]. Coordination: share persona and fake-job-site indicators with force protection and OPSEC offices for awareness training on long-duration social engineering [S3][S5][S6].

provenance.importedSummary: A previously undocumented attack group is using both custom and off-the-shelf malware to target IT providers in Saudi Arabia in what appear to be supply chain attacks with the end goal of compromising the IT providers’ customers. The group, which we are calling Tortoiseshell, has been active since at least July 2018. Symantec has identified a total of 11 organizations hit by the group, the majority of which are based in Saudi Arabia. In at least two organizations, evidence suggests that the attackers gained domain admin-level access.
